candidate.title: BLESS
candidate.scope: The single BLESS row of the assigned Illumina DNA poster, expanded there as breaks labeling and enrichment on streptavidin and sequencing, interpreted using Crosetto et al. (2013) Figure 1 and Online Methods. It depicts one route from exposed genomic DSB ends through proximal labeling, fragmentation, affinity capture and distal labeling to released amplified DNA. Proximal/distal primer captions refer to linker components of BLESS. The adjacent SSB-Seq and DSB-Seq rows and the partially visible Rep-Seq/MAF row are separately named catalogue assays, not alternatives targeted by this BLESS card. The candidate collection page has the matching BLESS heading and schematic captions. The drawn random-shearing label is retained alongside the primary implementation’s HaeIII fragmentation resolution. Sequencing interpretation is explained at the final material interface; unshown platform preparation, computational settings and related-assay adaptations are outside this extraction.

states.label: Genome DNA bearing exposed double-strand break ends
features: Biological target: exposed genomic double-strand break ends, identified by the Double-strand break icon; the yellow target mark is explanatory.
Although captioned Genome DNA, the initial tagging substrate is genomic DNA in fixed, purified intact nuclei in the primary implementation; DNA extraction occurs after tagging.
At the ligation interface, the primary paper reports blunt, 5′-phosphorylated DSB ends. End preparation is input history, not a separately drawn operation.

evidence.locator: BLESS route start: Genome DNA, blue duplex with a double-strand discontinuity.
BLESS left identification panel: Double-strand break and Breaks labeling and enrichment on streptavidin and sequencing (BLESS). Yellow mark identifies the target; it is not a reagent-addition step.

evidence.quote: After purification of intact nuclei, DSBs are blunted, 5′-phosphorylated, and finally ligated to a biotinylated linker (proximal) using the highly specific T4 ligase enzyme, which can only ligate double-stranded but not single-stranded breaks.
After fixation to stabilize chromatin and prevent artificial DSBs, cells are lysed and shortly incubated with proteinase K to purify intact nuclei.

states.label: Biotinylated proximal primer / proximal linker
features: Poster calls this a primer; the primary paper identifies the material as a hairpin-like double-stranded proximal linker that is ligated to genomic DNA.

Covalently attached biotin supplies the streptavidin-capture handle. The blue terminal symbol in the poster is interpreted from the explicit biotinylated label and paper, not as a chemical structural formula.
A proximal-specific barcode at the ligatable boundary marks the genomic junction; an I-SceI recognition site enables later linker cleavage.

evidence.locator: BLESS: Biotinylated proximal primer, orange duplex/loop-like linker with a blue terminal symbol, supplied at the first ligation arrow.

evidence.quote: The linker forms a hairpin-like structure, and thus can be ligated to either a blunt DSB or to an identical linker molecule, but cannot form concatemers. The ligatable end of the linker consists of a barcode sequence marking the exact position of ligation followed by the XhoI recognition site.

Both proximal (P) and distal (D) linkers share an XhoI site (yellow), the I-SceI endonuclease minimal recognition site (non-highlighted letters), and a seven-thymine loop (bold). Each linker contains a specific barcode sequence marking the ligation site (orange and brown). The proximal linker is biotinylated (orange oval).

DSBs are ligated in situ to a proximal linker (red arch) covalently linked to biotin (orange oval) (1), gDNA is extracted and fragmented (2), and labeled fragments are captured on streptavidin beads (gray ovals) (3).

states.label: Released, PCR-amplified DSB-flanking DNA for downstream sequencing
features: I-SceI cleavage releases captured DNA, followed by amplification using linker-specific primers; the final poster icon is a generic DNA duplex.
Readout carrier: genomic DNA adjacent to a proximal-linker-marked processed break end, with proximal/distal barcode context retained for identifying correctly tagged fragments.
The genomic sequence next to the proximal ligation boundary supports mapping the captured end. The distal end reflects fragmentation, not a second pre-existing biological DSB.
The poster stops at amplified DNA. Platform library construction and sequencing are downstream interfaces; this icon alone does not establish an Illumina adapter-complete library.
The assay captures available unjoined ends at a snapshot. Accessible telomere ends can be represented, and fixation-related artifacts and background limit biological specificity.

operations.label: Ligate primer
operations.description: Ligate the biotinylated proximal DNA linker to a prepared genomic DSB end in situ, producing genomic DNA bearing a covalently attached proximal label and biotin handle. The poster label primer denotes the incorporated linker here.
operations.mechanism: T4 DNA ligase joins the proximal linker to blunt, 5′-phosphorylated double-stranded ends in purified nuclei, as reported by the primary paper.
operations.information_effect: Introduces a physical proximal-barcode/genomic-end junction and a biotin capture handle before extraction. The tag marks the processed ligation position rather than preserving every original overhang nucleotide.

operations.label: DNA isolation and random shearing
operations.description: Extract the previously labeled genomic DNA and fragment it, generating a mixture in which a subset of fragments retains the proximal linker, biotin and adjacent genomic sequence. The drawn label random shearing is preserved. For the cited 2013 implementation, fragmentation is specifically HaeIII digestion; c_fragmentation records this source discrepancy.
operations.mechanism: Schematic-level transformation: isolation and fragmentation after in situ tagging. Primary implementation: purified gDNA is fragmented with HaeIII restriction enzyme, rather than physical shearing.
operations.information_effect: Retains the tagged original break boundary while generating a distal end used for the second linker. The newly produced fragmentation ends do not thereby become evidence of biological DSBs.

operations.label: Capture on streptavidin beads
operations.description: Enrich the labeled fragments from the extracted DNA mixture by binding their proximal biotin handle to streptavidin beads. The selected output is bead-attached genomic DNA, with unlabeled fragments depicted as faded background.
operations.mechanism: Affinity attachment of the proximal-linker biotin to streptavidin beads; streptavidin is the capture support, not an incorporated sequencing tag.
operations.information_effect: Selects the physical label installed before extraction and carries the associated genomic sequence forward. Affinity retention alone does not establish perfect biological specificity.

operations.label: Digest with I-SceI and PCR
operations.description: Digest the linker-bearing captured fragments with I-SceI to release DNA from the biotin/streptavidin attachment, then amplify the released fragments with linker-specific primers. These sequential actions remain one operation block because the poster combines them and provides no intervening material boundary.
operations.mechanism: I-SceI cleaves sites in the linkers; released genomic fragments are PCR-amplified. This is library-fragment release, distinct from using I-SceI to induce a biological break in validation experiments.
operations.information_effect: Produces amplified DNA carrying genomic sequence associated with the tagged break boundary. Subsequent sequencing can map those ends from linker/genome junctions; it does not report all breaks that occurred and were repaired before labeling. The diagram does not show sequencing or platform library construction as additional operations.

method_scopes.rationale: All five local operation instances follow the arrows within the BLESS row and apply to the in situ proximal-linker tagging implementation described by Crosetto et al. The scope preserves the poster’s fragmentation depiction and records the paper’s HaeIII implementation separately in c_fragmentation. Extracted DNA is produced after proximal ligation, so capture and distal ligation retain that input history. No mixing or alternative workflow is depicted. Paper-associated SaCas9 use remains an application reference; GUIDE-seq and LAM-HTGTS remain comparisons. The combined digestion/PCR caption is one broad local block, with release before amplification established by Figure 1a.
